title: Gateway quota rollback: safety net and operator playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: After an automated quota rollback triggered during a sustained traffic spike, the gateway entered a state where partially-applied quota rules allowed short-lived token-level bursts that produced a 429 storm for downstream services. This ticket captures technical root cause findings, fixes that were applied, and a formal operator playbook + safety-net automation to avoid repeat incidents.
timeline: 2026-03-01 01:12 UTC — Increased traffic from partner integration; quota rollback automation triggered due to perceived overcommit on dedicated pools.
2026-03-01 01:18 UTC — Partial rollback applied: routing rules updated but token lease cache not cleared, leading to mismatch between enforcer and gateway view of remaining quota.
2026-03-01 01:22 UTC — Burst of 429s observed across us-west region; on-call flagged outage and paged SRE.
2026-03-01 01:32 UTC — Emergency throttle stabilization: disabled automatic rollback and enabled conservative global cap; 429 rate declined but latency increased for queued requests.
2026-03-01 04:10 UTC — Post-incident triage started; initial fix deploy at 06:20 UTC included explicit auth-lease invalidation and retry-backoff safety in the gateway SDK.
2026-03-02 09:00 UTC — Root cause confirmed: rollback path did not invalidate sharded token caches and introduced temporary token misattribution.
investigation_notes: Root cause: rollback automation mutated routing rules asynchronously while relying on eventual cache eviction. The enforcer used an in-memory shard index for token quotas; when routing changed, the index still returned old lease states for ~30-90s, allowing bursts.
Race window: ~T+6s to T+90s depending on KV cache TTL and shard rebalancing. Short TTLs masked issue in some zones; longer TTLs amplified it.

Contributing factor: rollback logic lacked a two-phase commit — no lease drain or circuit check before flipping routing rules. No explicit topology versioning header was used between gateway and enforcer.
Mitigation already deployed: added synchronous invalidation RPC for token shards on rollback path; introduced topology-version header to reject requests from mismatched views.
Observability gaps: dashboards showed 429 but did not surface correlation with rollback jobs. Added metric: rollback.job_active{job_id} and rollback.topology_version mismatch gauge.
action_items: A1: Implement coordinated rollback protocol (two-phase): prepare -> invalidate token shards -> commit routing change. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2026-03-21.

A2: Add an automatic circuit probe that, after any automated rollback, issues low-rate canary requests across shards and blocks commit if probe sees >1% 429. Owner: SRE team (lead: Marco Ruiz). Due: 2026-03-18.
A3: Backfill topology-version header across gateway <-> enforcer RPCs and fail-fast on mismatches. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-12 (partial done), full rollout by 2026-03-20.

A4: Create operator playbook: detection alerts, immediate temp mitigations (disable rollback, enable global cap, trigger shard purge RPC), and postmortem checklist. Owner: On-call tooling (Asha Patel). Due: 2026-03-14.
A5: Add rollout guard: automated rollback requires approval if active customer commit > X QPS for the affected pool. Owner: Product (runtime). Due: 2026-04-01.
A6: Dashboard improvements: correlate rollback jobs to 429 spikes and surface impacted customer tokens. Owner: Observability (R&D). Due: 2026-03-25.
A7: Run chaos tests simulating stale shard caches during rollout for next two capacity cycles. Owner: Reliability tests. Due: 2026-04-10.
A8: Post-deployment verification job: 24h automated smoke that validates token consumption trends after any routing change. Owner: CI/CD. Due: 2026-03-28.
A9: Documentation: update engineering runbooks and create a short training session for Support and Solutions on the new playbook. Owner: Developer Experience. Due: 2026-03-31.
